vulnerability.title: Set SSH Daemon LogLevel to VERBOSE
vulnerability.description: The VERBOSE parameter configures the SSH daemon to record login and logout activity. To specify the log level in SSH, add or correct the following line in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-complianceascode-hardening.conf: LogLevel VERBOSE
vulnerability.recommendation: Remediation script: # Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms if rpm --quiet -q kernel-core; then mkdir -p /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d touch /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-complianceascode-hardening.conf chmod 0600 /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-complianceascode-hardening.conf LC_ALL=C sed -i "/^\s*LogLevel\s\+/Id" "/etc/ssh/sshd_config" LC_ALL=C sed -i "/^\s*LogLevel\s\+/Id" "/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d"/*.conf if [ -e "/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-complianceascode-hardening.conf" ] ; then LC_ALL=C sed -i "/^\s*LogLevel\s\+/Id" "/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-complianceascode-hardening.conf" else touch "/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-complianceascode-hardening.conf" fi # make sure file has newline at the end sed -i -e '$a\' "/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-complianceascode-hardening.conf" cp "/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/00-complianceascode

triage_decision.reason: The remediation only edits or creates a small SSH configuration fragment to set LogLevel VERBOSE, a standard STIG recommendation. It does not modify authentication mechanisms, kernel parameters, or boot-critical files, and the change is unlikely to cause lockout. A service restart may be needed but poses minimal risk.
triage_decision.estimated_impact: authentication/authorization affected; Service restart may briefly interrupt active SSH sessions; Incorrect syntax could prevent sshd from starting

previous_review_verdicts.feedback: The plan will set LogLevel VERBOSE in a dedicated drop‑in file and restart sshd, which satisfies the requirement. Minor enhancements could improve robustness and reduce impact.
concerns: If other sshd configuration files already contain a LogLevel directive, duplicates may remain, which could cause confusion about which setting is applied.
Restarting sshd may briefly interrupt active SSH sessions.
The plan does not explicitly ensure the file ends with a newline, which some tools expect.
suggested_improvements: Remove any existing LogLevel lines from /etc/ssh/sshd_config and other *.conf files in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d before adding the compliant line.
Append a newline to the file after modifications (e.g., `sed -i -e '$a\'`).
Consider using `systemctl reload sshd` instead of a full restart to avoid disconnecting users.
Add a verification step that checks the effective sshd configuration (`ssh -T -f /etc/ssh/sshd_config` or `sshd -T`) to confirm LogLevel is VERBOSE.

previous_review_verdicts.feedback: The plan correctly removes any existing LogLevel directives, creates a dedicated drop‑in with the required LogLevel VERBOSE, reloads the sshd service, and verifies the effective setting. If executed as written it will remediate the vulnerability.
concerns: The glob '/etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/*.conf' may expand to the literal pattern when no files exist, causing sed to error.
Using 'systemctl try-reload-or-restart' could trigger a full service restart if reload fails, potentially disconnecting active sessions.
The sed expression also deletes commented LogLevel lines, which removes useful documentation.
suggested_improvements: Guard the glob by checking for matching files before running sed, e.g., 'shopt -s nullglob' or a conditional loop.
Prefer 'systemctl reload sshd' when a reload is sufficient, or document the risk of a restart.
